title: Vertra API product (apis/<name>/api.yaml, kind: Api), format v2
description: A backend the team already runs, published through the install's gateway. Its OpenAPI file is the allowlist: the gateway forwards only requests whose method and path it describes and whose parameters, headers and body fit its schemas, and blocks everything else.

apiVersion.description: The catalog format: vertra.dev/v2. A file without it is from before v2: ./vertra catalog migrate rewrites it.

name.description: Its folder's name, apis/<name>/: callers reach it at /<team>/<name>/ on the gateway.

spec.description: Its OpenAPI file (3.0 or 3.1, YAML or JSON), beside api.yaml. Every operation in it is what may reach the backend; nothing else does.

backend.description: Where the gateway forwards to, and how it signs in there. The URL's host must be one this install's admins allow, or the API is held, not published.

url.description: The backend's base URL, https (http only for a Service inside the cluster); the spec's servers must include it.

auth.description: The credential the gateway adds to each request, minted per request where it can be. Left out: none (the backend checks Vertra-Caller, or nothing).

serviceAccountToken.description: A token for the API's own Kubernetes ServiceAccount, for this audience: for a backend in a cluster that checks Kubernetes tokens.

googleIdToken.description: A Google ID token for the backend (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, IAP), minted per request through the API ServiceAccount's federation: as serviceAccount, for audience (default: backend.url).

secret.description: A fallback for a backend that only takes a static key: a team secret, read by name per request, sent in header (with scheme before it, e.g. Bearer).

serviceAccount.description: The Kubernetes ServiceAccount, in the team's namespace, the gateway mints this API's backend credentials for (the console creates it). It ends in -api: the gateway may mint tokens for those ServiceAccounts and no others. Left out: <name>-api.

shareWith.description: The other teams that may call it, or ["*"] for every team. Left out, only its own team.

visibility.description: listed (the default): every team sees it, and those it isn't shared with can ask for access. hidden: only its own team sees it, so it can't have shareWith.

deprecated.description: Marks it deprecated, saying what to use instead. It keeps working; the console shows the message to everyone who uses it.

reachable.description: cluster (the default): the gateway answers for it inside the cluster only. internet: also on the gateway's public address, if this install lets the team publish there.

limits.description: Requests per calling team, per minute or second: default for every team, and any team by name.

timeout.description: How long the gateway waits for the backend's answer to begin, 1s to 300s (default 30s).

maxRequest.description: The largest request body it forwards, up to 10MiB (default 1MiB).
